akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is: "your hatefulness is great as hatefulness" (كَبُرَ مَقْتُكُم مَقْتاً); then He said ﴿أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا لاَ تَفْعَلُونَ﴾, that is: your saying (قولُكم).

akhfash:13-13.t: [And] He said ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَهَا﴾: He means "and another trade" (وتجارةٌ أُخْرَى).

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سَبَّحَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; and ﴿ما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ما في السموات». ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and two khabars (predicates), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ «أيّ» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «أيها»; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿لِمَ﴾ «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what comes after them; ﴿تَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ negating [particle] and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿كَبُرَ﴾ a past verb; ﴿مَقْتاً﴾ tamyīz (specification); ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «كبر..» is its fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ negating [particle] and an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿يُحِبُّ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿يُقاتِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فِي سَبِيلِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿صَفًّا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيانٌ﴾ «كأنّ», its noun and its khabar; ﴿مَرْصُوصٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قالَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, «إذ» is an adverb of time, and a past verb; ﴿مُوسى﴾ its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لِقَوْمِهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿يا قَوْمِ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), in the accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which has been dropped for lightness; ﴿لِمَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what comes after them, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿تُؤْذُونَنِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil, the nūn being for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿قَدْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) and an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿أَنِّي﴾ «أنّ» and its noun; ﴿رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ its khabar (predicate), annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to «رسول», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أنّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «تعلمون». And the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya); ﴿زاغُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a genitive by iḍāfa; ﴿أَزاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil; ﴿قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi; and the clause «فلما..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Translator's note: the quoted word is printed with a kasra in the source; in the verse it is «وَاللَّهُ», nominative.]»; ﴿لا يَهْدِي﴾ negating [particle] and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْفاسِقِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قالَ عِيسَى﴾ the i'rab of its like has been given before; ﴿ابْنُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «عيسى», and ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to «إسرائيل», in the accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ «إنّ», its noun and its khabar (predicate), which is annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رسول», and the nominal clause is the object of the saying; ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿لِما﴾ both are attached to «مصدقا»; ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to ﴿يَدَيَّ﴾; ﴿مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وَمُبَشِّراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «مصدقا»; ﴿بِرَسُولٍ﴾ both are attached to «مبشرا»; ﴿يَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول»; ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِي﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar, and the clause is a second naʿt of «رسول». ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لِما﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya) «[Translator's note: the source prints «لِما» here; the word in the verse is «لَمّا».]»; ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by iḍāfa; ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿هذا سِحْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ a naʿt, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying, and the clause «قالوا..» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «لما», with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِمَّنِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم»; ﴿افْتَرى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿يُدْعى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent; ﴿إِلَى الْإِسْلامِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «هو», and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the i'rab of its like has been given before.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لِيُطْفِؤُا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose (lām al-taʿlīl), the wāw being its fāʿil; ﴿نُورَ اللَّهِ﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to the Name of Majesty; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿بِأَفْواهِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿اللَّهُ مُتِمُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿نُورِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لَوْ كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ﴾ «لو» is concessive-connective (waṣliyya), and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَرْسَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿رَسُولَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; ﴿بِالْهُدى﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَدِينِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الهدى»; ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit «أن» after the lām of purpose, the hāʾ being its mafʿūl bihi and the fāʿil latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are attached to «أرسل»; ﴿عَلَى الدِّينِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿كُلِّهِ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿لَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ﴾ «لو» is concessive-connective (waṣliyya), and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before, and ﴿هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ﴾ «هل» is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿عَلى تِجارَةٍ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿تُنْجِيكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «تجارة»; ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ a naʿt of «عذاب».

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَتُجاهِدُونَ﴾ conjoined to «تؤمنون»; ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿بِأَمْوالِكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb as well; ﴿وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ conjoined to «أموالكم»; ﴿ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to «خير»; ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ «إن» is conditional and makes the verb jussive, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the tāʾ being its noun; ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «كنتم», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it falls as the answer to the command understood from His saying «تؤمنون بالله», the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ذُنُوبَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause has no grammatical position; ﴿وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يغفر لكم»; ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and an imperfect verb «[Translator's note: «and an imperfect verb» evidently refers to «تَجْرِي», which is not quoted in the source.]»; ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات»; ﴿وَمَساكِنَ﴾ conjoined to «جنات»; ﴿طَيِّبَةً﴾ a naʿt of «مساكن»; ﴿فِي جَنَّاتِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَدْنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ a naʿt, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَأُخْرى﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), the fronted khabar (predicate) being omitted; ﴿تُحِبُّونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «أخرى»; ﴿نَصْرٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نصر»; ﴿وَفَتْحٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «نصر»; ﴿قَرِيبٌ﴾ a naʿt of «فتح»; ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿كُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, the wāw being its noun; ﴿أَنْصارَ اللَّهِ﴾ its khabar (predicate), annexed to the Name of Majesty, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿كَما﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿قالَ عِيسَى﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ابْنُ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «عيسى»; ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿لِلْحَوارِيِّينَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «ما» and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the kāf; ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَنْصارِي﴾ khabar; ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿نَحْنُ أَنْصارُ اللَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿فَآمَنَتْ طائِفَةٌ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْ بَنِي﴾ both are attached to an omitted naʿt of «طائفة»; ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿وَكَفَرَتْ طائِفَةٌ﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَيَّدْنَا الَّذِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil, the relative noun being its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلى عَدُوِّهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا ظاهِرِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أصبح», its noun and its khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿هَلْ أَدُلُّكمْ عَلَىٰ تِجَارَةٍ تُنجِيكُم مِّنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: آمنوا. Had it been said in our reading: أن تؤمنوا [it would have been valid], because it is an explanation (tarjama) of the trade. When you explain a preceding noun by a verb, it is permissible both to include أن and to omit it: you say to a man: هل لك فى خير تقوم بنا إلى المسجد فنصلى (would you like something good: you go with us to the mosque and we pray), and if you said: أن تقوم إلى المسجد it would be correct. Similar to this — where something explains what precedes it in two ways — is His saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإِنسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ﴾: أَنَّا and إِنَّا. Whoever says أَنَّا here is like the one who puts (أَنْ) before يقوم, and whoever says إِنَّا is like the one who drops (أنْ) from تقوم. Similar to it is: ﴿عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا﴾ and (إِنَّا).

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾.
It is put in the jussive in our reading because of هل; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh because of the overt imperative, namely His saying (آمِنوا). The import of هل أدلكم is also a command in meaning, like your saying to a man: هل أنت ساكت؟ (will you be quiet?), whose meaning is: be quiet. And Allah knows best.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأُخْرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَهَا﴾.
It is in the position of the nominative, i.e.: and you have another [thing] in this world besides the reward of the Hereafter. Then He said: ﴿نَصْرٌ مِّن ٱللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ﴾, which explains the "other". Had it been نصرا من الله [in the accusative], it would have been correct; and had it been said: وآخر تحبونه, meaning the victory and the help, it would have been correct.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿كُونُوۤاْ أَنصَارَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd read it in the genitive construct, and the people of Medina read it: أنصاراً الله, leaving الأنصار unattached and not putting it in a construct. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: أنتم أنصار الله.
[Translator's note: «أنصاراً الله» is as printed; the Medinan reading is أنصاراً لله.]

farraa:2-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لاَ تَفْعَلُونَ﴾.
The Muslims used to say: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them, even if our lives and our wealth were lost in it. Then when the battle of Uḥud took place, they turned away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he was wounded in the head and his front tooth was broken; so He said: ﴿لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لاَ تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ because of that. Then He said: ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ [أَن تَقُولُواْ﴾. أن is in the position of the nominative, because كبر is like your saying: بئس رجلاً أخوك (how bad a man is your brother). And His saying: كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عند الله]: He has concealed in كبر a noun which is nominative. As for His saying ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلمة﴾, al-Ḥasan read it with the nominative [كلمةٌ], because he did not conceal anything [in the verb] and assigned the verb to كلمة; and whoever reads it in the accusative has concealed in كبرت a noun intended as nominative.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَانٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ﴾: [joined] with lead (raṣāṣ); He is urging them to fight.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ﴾.
Yaḥyā or al-Aʿmash — al-Farrāʾ was unsure which — read it: "والله متمُّ نورِه" with the genitive construct (iḍāfa), and the people of the Hijaz read it with tanwīn: متمٌّ نورَه. Both are correct.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṣaff (The Ranks)
Makkan
﷽
﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ وهو العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾ — we have already explained what is in His saying: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ﴾.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ — the original is ”لِما“; the alif was elided because "mā" and the lām are like a single thing, and the use of ”ما“ with the lām in questions became frequent. If you pause on it you say ”لِمَهْ“, but one does not pause on it that way in the Quran, lest the muṣḥaf be contradicted; the reciter ought to join it (to what follows). This was said to them because they had said: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, we would do them, even if it meant losing our lives and our wealth." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿هَلْ أدُلُّكم عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكم مِن عَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 10] up to His saying: ﴿وَتُجاهِدُونَ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأمْوالِكم وأنْفُسِكم ذَلِكم خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 11]. Then, when the day of ”أُحُدٍ“ (Uḥud) came, those who turned away from the Prophet ﷺ turned away, until his front tooth was broken and he was wounded in his face; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ ﴿كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أنْ تَقُولُوا ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 3]. ”أنْ تَقُولُوا“ is in the position of the nominative, and ”مَقْتًا“ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification). The meaning is: "Your saying what you do not do is grievous as an object of loathing in the sight of Allah." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known what He loves, and said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ في سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأنَّهم بُنْيانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 4], i.e. a structure whose parts cleave to one another, no part of it leaving another. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He loves whoever stands firm in jihad in His way and keeps to his place like the chambers of a compact building. It is also possible — and Allah knows best — that He meant that their intentions be equal in fighting their enemy, so that in unity of purpose and mutual alliance they are like a compact structure.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ يا قَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِي وقَدْ تَعْلَمُونَ أنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ — we have explained in Sūrat ”اَلْأحْزابِ“ (al-Aḥzāb) the ways in which they had harmed him. ﴿فَلَمّا زاغُوا أزاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ means: they deviated from the truth and turned away from it, so Allah led them astray and turned their hearts aside.

His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي القَوْمَ الفاسِقِينَ﴾ means: He does not guide one whom it is already in His knowledge that he is a transgressor.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ — the position of ”إذْ قالَ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ“ and of ”إذْ قالَ مُوسى“ alike is accusative. The meaning is: "Remember when Mūsā said, and remember when ʿĪsā son of Maryam said," i.e. recall to your people and your community the story of Mūsā and ʿĪsā, and what the end was of those who believed in them, and the end of those who disbelieved and harmed the prophets.

His saying: ﴿لِلْحَوارِيِّينَ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 14] — it is said that the disciples (al-ḥawāriyyūn) were so called because of the whiteness of their clothes; and it is said that they were fullers. ”اَلْحَوارِيُّونَ“ are the sincere intimates of the prophets and their elect, and the evidence for that is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «"Al-Zubayr is my paternal aunt's son and my disciple (ḥawāriyy) from my community,"» and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are disciples. The interpretation of ”اَلْحَوارِيُّونَ“ in the language is: those who have been purified and cleansed of every defect. Likewise ”اَلدَّقِيقُ الحُوّارى“ (fine white flour) comes from this; it was only so called because it is sifted from the kernel of the wheat and its pure part. Its interpretation with regard to people is that he is the one who, when his selection is reviewed time after time, is found free of defects. The root of ”اَلتَّحْوِيرُ“ in the language is from ”حارَ، يَحُورُ“, which is returning and repeating. This is its interpretation — and Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿مَن أنْصارِي إلى اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 14] means: "Who are my helpers together with Allah?" And some said: "Who are my helpers towards the help of Allah?" The poet said:
؎وَلَوْحُ ذِراعَيْنِ في بِرْكَةٍ ∗∗∗ إلى جُؤْجُؤٍ رَهِلِ المَنكِبِ
(And the broad flat of two forelegs in a chest, together with a breastbone, slack of shoulder.)
The meaning is ”اَلْكاهِلُ مَعَ جُؤْجُؤِ رَهَلِ المَنكِبِ“ (the withers together with a breastbone slack of shoulder). [Translator's note: the gloss uses الكاهل, a word not found in the verse as quoted; it is translated as written.]

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكم ذُنُوبَكم ويُدْخِلْكم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ ومَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً في جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ — this is the jawāb (apodosis) of ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ وتُجاهِدُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 11], because its meaning is the meaning of a command. The meaning is: "Believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives; He will forgive you your sins," i.e. if you do that He will forgive you. The evidence for that is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ”آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ“. Some grammarians erred and said: this is the answer to ”هَلْ“. This is a clear error: it is not the case that when the Prophet guides them to what benefits them Allah forgives them; Allah forgives them only when they believe and strive. So it is the answer to "تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ، وتُجاهِدُونَ، يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ". As for the jussive (majzūm) answer to a question, it is like your saying ”هَلْ جِئْتَنِي بِشَيْءٍ أُعْطِكَ مِثْلَهُ“ (have you brought me something, so that I may give you the like of it), the meaning being: "had you brought me (something) I would have given you," and "if you bring me (something) I will give you"; and likewise ”أيْنَ بَيْتُكَ أزُرْكَ“ (where is your house, that I may visit you).

His saying: ﴿فِي جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ means: in gardens of residence and permanence. One says ”عَدَنَ بِالمَكانِ“ when one has settled in a place.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأُخْرى تُحِبُّونَها نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ﴾ — the meaning is: "And you have another transaction which you love, and it is help from Allah and a near victory." If you wish, it is nominative as a badal (substitute) for ”أُخْرى“; the meaning is: "He will admit you to gardens, and you will have help from Allah and a near victory."

His saying: ﴿إنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إلَيْكم مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 6] — ”مُصَدِّقًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "I am the Messenger of Allah to you, in a state of confirming the Torah which preceded me, and in a state of giving glad tidings of a messenger" ﴿يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أحْمَدُ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 6]. It was read with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, ”مِن بَعْدِيَ“, and with the yāʾ quiescent and dropped from pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; but in writing it is retained: ”مِن بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أحْمَدُ“. The preferred choice according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl is to vowel this yāʾ with a fatḥa.

As for whoever read ”يَغْفِر لَّكُمْ“, assimilating the rāʾ into the lām, that is not permissible in recitation according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, because according to the two of them the rāʾ is not assimilated into the lām. Yet it has been transmitted from an imam of great standing in recitation, namely Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, and I do not reckon that he recited it except having heard it from the Arabs. Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and all the Basrans — except Abū ʿAmr — held that the lām is assimilated into the rāʾ, and that the rāʾ is not assimilated into the lām. The argument of those who said that the rāʾ is not assimilated into the lām is that the rāʾ is a strong, trilled letter, and if the rāʾ is assimilated into the lām its trill is lost. Their proof that it has an advantage over other letters in firmness is that you do not apply imāla (inclination of the vowel towards i) to a word of the pattern ”فاعِلٌ“ when at its beginning there is one of the velarized (iṭbāq) or elevated (mustaʿliya) letters. These are seven letters: four of them velarized, namely ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ, and three elevated, namely khāʾ, ghayn and qāf. You do not say ”هَذا صالِحٌ“ inclining the ṣād towards kasra; but if in the position of the lām there is a rāʾ, the kasra (imāla) is allowed: you say ”هَذا صارِمٌ“. And you do not say ”مَرَرْتُ بِضابِطٍ“ with imāla of the ḍād, but you do say ”مَرَرْتُ بِضارِبٍ“, for the rāʾ with kasra lowers the vowel of the velarized ṣād and ḍād. This chapter — the chapter of imāla — is one in grammar that the Basrans alone treated; the Kufans and the Medinans have nothing on it.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أنْصارَ اللَّهِ﴾ — most of the reading is ”كُونُوا أنْصارَ اللَّهِ“, and it is the preferred choice because of their saying ”نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ“; because the two verses are in answer to ”كُونُوا أنْصارًا لِلَّهِ“: ”نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ“. And it is possible for ”نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ“ to be an answer to that. [Translator's note: the reasoning is compressed in the text as transmitted; the point is that the reading أنصارَ الله matches the disciples' reply نحن أنصارُ الله, while the variant أنصارًا لله can also be answered by it.] And ﴿واللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 8] was also read ”واللَّهُ مُتِمٌّ نُورَهُ“; both are good.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأيَّدْنا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلى عَدُوِّهِمْ﴾ — the meaning of ”أيَّدْنا“ is: We strengthened; its derivation is from ”اَلْأيْدُ“, and ”اَلْأيْدُ“ is strength.
